resolvedFindings.issue: Root clean environment cannot assume trust of runner-owned checkout
resolvedFindings.resolution: Exact ROOT and ROOT/.git safe.directory arguments for source rev-parse and clone; no global or wildcard trust.

resolvedFindings.issue: Parent Docker commands inherited GitHub read token
resolvedFindings.resolution: Serial run defaults remove GH_TOKEN and GITHUB_TOKEN before child creation and restore parent afterwards; only three explicit GitHub metadata/download calls opt in. Real subprocess synthetic-token regression passed.

reviewedControls: Fixed same-repository PR branch, label and first attempt; exact checked-out head; read-only workflow permissions.
Seven historical ZIP metadata pins before and after transfer plus exact byte size/digest; original source and candidate-set pins.
New private root-owned directory and owned cgroup with read-back process memory 3 GiB, swap zero, pids 128 and 2 CPU quota.
Shared worker command deadline; outer timeout, process-domain cleanup before bounded daemon cleanup.
Unknown load retains durable claim and owned directory with unverified cleanup; no retry.
Known complete receipt permits only five exact original tags absent from before-image inventory; live identity inspection, no force, image-ID deletion or prune.
Token removed from non-GitHub children; whitelisted bounded report files; no application services started.
limitations: Actual GitHub artifact availability, Linux controllers, disk capacity and Docker load remain to be verified in CI.
Docker daemon is outside the process cgroup; 3 GiB is not a Docker daemon memory bound.
This preflight/load workflow does not start five services, run six business journeys, refresh release proof or establish production readiness.
Unknown Docker load is deliberately unverified and retained; successful-path cleanup is not a guarantee after arbitrary job termination.
